title: Pseudo Entropy in Quantum Spin Chains: from Integrability to Chaos
authors: Tara Bahadur Rana, Yadav Raj Dahal, Kiran Adhikari
abstract: In this work, we study pseudo entropy and spectral dynamics in quantum spin chains (Heisenberg XXZ model and the mixed-field Ising model) to investigate whether they can serve as diagnostics of quantum chaos. First, we derive an exact relation between the real part of the thermal pseudo entropy and the spectral form factor. This provided evidence that pseudo entropy could exhibit the characteristic dip, logarithmic ramp, and plateau, implying the precise manner in which pseudo entropy probes chaos. We found that the imaginary part, while it does not diagnose chaos, can still provide crucial information about Fisher zeros that is not available in the real counterpart. For spatial pseudo entropy in the XXZ chain, we find that the logarithmic critical scaling persists in both integrable and chaotic regimes, and that the non-positivity conjecture holds. Finally, we derive an exact connection between pseudo entropy, relative pseudo entropy, and spectral complexity with a potential connection to holography.
summary: This work develops and applies the concept of pseudo entropy to study quantum chaos in spin chains. By analyzing how pseudo entropy evolves, the authors successfully distinguish between integrable and chaotic dynamics, showing that the real part exhibits a characteristic signature of chaos. This framework also connects to spectral complexity and suggests potential applications in quantum gravity and holography.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether 'pseudo entropy' can serve as a diagnostic tool to distinguish between quantum chaotic and integrable regimes in quantum spin chains.
main_result: The real part of the pseudo entropy exhibits the characteristic dip, logarithmic ramp, and plateau structure associated with quantum chaos, while critical scaling persists across both integrable and chaotic regimes.
method: The study employs the definition of pseudo entropy, derived from the von Neumann entropy of transition matrices, and relates its real part to the Spectral Form Factor (SFF).
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum spin chains, specifically the Heisenberg XXZ model and the mixed-field Ising model, which are deformed by adding next-to-nearest-neighbor interactions.
key_observables: Pseudo entropy (thermal and spatial), Spectral Form Factor (SFF), and spectral complexity.
important_parameters: The deformation strength $\alpha$ controlling the transition from integrable ($\alpha=0$) to chaotic ($\alpha=1$) behavior.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving exact relations connecting pseudo entropy, relative pseudo entropy, and spectral complexity, and assumes the applicability of holographic concepts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate level spacing distributions showing Poisson (integrable) vs. Wigner-Dyson (chaotic) statistics, and the time evolution of the pseudo entropy term exhibiting the characteristic dip-ramp-plateau structure in the chaotic case.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining pseudo entropy and relating its real part to the SFF. It then applies this diagnostic tool to the XXZ chain, showing the transition from Poisson to GOE statistics. Finally, it establishes deeper connections between pseudo entropy, relative pseudo entropy, and spectral complexity, suggesting holographic implications.
why_interesting: The use of entanglement-like measures (pseudo entropy) to diagnose fundamental quantum dynamics (chaos vs. integrability) provides a powerful, quantifiable tool applicable to many-body systems beyond standard spectral analysis.
